On Mon, Nov 15, 2026 at 10:03 AM, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks Jane — received. Looping in Monica (Legal) and Lauren (Sales Ops) to confirm next steps.

Quick summary after initial review:
- Acme's notice is adequate as notice but the MSA requires that Acme provide an opportunity for Redwood to object to any subprocessor that will have access to customer data. We should request the business justification and limit of access in writing.
- The attached Acme-signed DPA is mostly acceptable, but we need the following edits before we execute or certify acceptance:
  * Explicit prohibition on using data for model training or re-use beyond logging/ops.
  * 30-day breach notification (we typically ask 72 hours for breaches affecting customer data; if vendor resists, we require an escalation path).
  * Clear flow-down of security obligations to any downstream subcontractors and audit rights (Section 6).
  * Data residency assurance for any EU data (if any) and subprocessors subject to standard SCCs as needed.
- Order Form: add a short clause that any change notice that adds a subprocessor who will have access to customer content triggers a written consent (or a 10-business-day silent approval window) — pick one based on product risk. I recommend requiring written consent where content access is possible.

I've attached a redlined MSA with suggested language (redlined_MSA_Redwood_20261116.docx) and a Subprocessor Notice template for Acme to complete. Please ask Acme to confirm the DataOcean subprocessor's SOC2 status and to provide a minimal business justification and list of technical controls.

If Acme can accept our edits in the DPA, we can do a quick DocuSign turnaround. If not, we should escalate to procurement for a commercial exception.

— Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
